label: On death
description: What happens when the unit is destroyed. A card has one or two.

terms.label: Respawn
terms.description: Nothing is left: the unit is simply gone. In a player version the player goes back to the buy screen (a remote operator goes back to their parked soldier).
terms.source_rule: In-game for a unit players drive in a game where they come back after it dies, including a vehicle whose crew die inside it. For a unit that is simply gone in the source, it is the proposal for infantry, organic units and uncrewed machines.

terms.label: Bail out
terms.description: The vehicle is destroyed and its crew eject as basic infantry with low health. Everyone inside gets out, passengers too.
terms.source_rule: In-game when the crew or riders get out on their own as the vehicle dies, even when only one gets out or only by chance. Jumping out by hand before it dies does not count; in our game that is the hold-X key every vehicle has. It is the proposal for any crewed machine outside the infantry class that is simply gone in the source.

terms.label: Wreck
terms.description: Leaves a wreck that teammates can repair or enemies can salvage.
terms.source_rule: In-game only when the remains stay on the field and a unit can repair, recrew or salvage them in the same match. Remains that only block the way or give cover do not count, nor do crates, weapons or loot that drop for pickup or for crafting later; put those in on_death.notes.

terms.label: Death blast
terms.description: Explodes on death, damaging everything nearby.
terms.source_rule: In-game only when the source says the explosion hurts units nearby, for this unit in its own title (for a series, its counted titles, as the Series games convention in docs/fields.md decides). A blast that is only for show, or a wreck that only hurts what it falls on, does not count.

terms.label: Pilot eject
terms.description: The pilot pops out in a light suit and can reach a new unit or a pickup.
terms.source_rule: In-game when the pilot leaves the wreck on their own as a unit that can keep fighting, such as walking to a new vehicle or a pickup. Ejecting by hand before the unit dies does not count.

tie_breaks.rule: A crewed vehicle that is simply gone in the source: bail-out, basis proposal. A vehicle players drive in a shooter whose crew die inside it: respawn, basis in-game, even when they could have jumped out by hand first.
Use two outcomes only when the source shows both, such as a husk that also explodes. Never pair a sourced outcome with the 3C default.

Pilot eject when the one who gets out is a pilot who, the sources say, can take a new vehicle or a pickup and keep fighting. Bail out when crew or riders get out as ordinary soldiers. Never code both for the same person.
